title: GTA 6 has secret playlists, and all you have to do is scan a few posters to unlock them
summary: Kodak Black and The Vault nightclub each have their own unique playlist.
body: Rockstar's lengthy credits reveal just how massive the GTA 6 song list truly is, but you don't start the game with every radio station unlocked. Leonida has two secret playlists (both needed for 100% completion), and neither is particularly hard to unlock once you know where to look. The Sniper of La Perle , Kodak Black's 22-track playlist, becomes available as soon as you scan four posters around La Perle at TWA Ponya Tattoo, Drip Drops, Aunt Zola's Soul Food, and the Jack of Hearts nightclub. Then there's The Vault Radio , which only requires you to scan a single poster at the nightclub of the same name. The Sniper of La Perle poster locations Head to La Perle and Crosstown to scan posters (Image: © Rockstar Games) This is in the northwestern corner of Vice-Dale County, between Stockyard and Rockridge. The shops automatically marked themselves on my map as I drove around La Perle and Crosstown, but I've included screenshots highlighting their specific locations in Vice City's Haitian district. Once you arrive at one, Jason or Lucia's phone should alert you to something nearby you can scan with a notification from the Waink It app. TWA Ponya Tattoo Look right as soon as you enter…

title: Despite GTA 6's huge map, it only takes about 4 minutes to fly across it in a plane
summary: Someone had to do it.
body: GTA 6's map is so big it's going to take months for people to comb through it and find everything. Rockstar has already posted the full map of Leonida online, but it doesn't answer one simple question that I know we've all been wondering: How long would it take to fly across this entire thing in a plane? The answer is a lot less time than it would take to go by car, but still long enough to give you an idea of the sheer scale we're working with here. Using the closest plane to Jason's house, my trip across Leonida took around 4 minutes and 18 seconds , which is a little under an hour of in-game time. You can watch the entire flight from start to finish below. Keep in mind that the Mammoth Dodo seaplane that carried me from the southern tip of the archipelago to the northern tip of the map is just one type of plane in GTA 6. I would bet there are faster options if you really want to zoom. Even though I'm still very early in the GTA 6's story, I didn't have to go too far out of my way to test this. Jason's house is conveniently located pretty close to a spot with perfectly unattended planes to borrow. The Sunbelt Highway that runs south of it will lead you right to the earliest plan…

title: Try this GTA 6 movement speed setting to make Jason and Lucia walk faster
summary: Pep up their step.
body: If you want to move faster in Grand Theft Auto 6, I can't blame you: There's a lot I've enjoyed about the opening hours I've spent in Jason's shoes. He's handy with a nailgun. He's a good sport when I make him wear the dumbest graphic tees I can find. For a gunslinging drug runner, he's a gentle soul. I just have one complaint. The man's got a leisurely gait. Which is fine! But there are plenty of times while roaming Leonida when you might wish he and Lucia were moving just a bit faster—just not so fast that you want to force them into a run. Luckily, Rockstar's got our back: There's a setting to bump up your basic movement speed without pushing a button. How to increase your movement speed in GTA 6 (Image credit: Rockstar) To change the pace that Jason and Lucia move at in GTA 6, head to Settings , move over to the Gameplay tab, and scroll down to the Movement section. The setting you're looking for is Movement Speed . This doesn't affect your top speed while sprinting and burning stamina. What it adjusts is the speed you move at when you fully push the joystick. There are four options, each one offering more speed than the last: Walk (the default), Fast Walk, Jog, and Run. It's …

title: GameStop boss calls for return of physical discs just as GTA 6 does digital gangbusters
summary: Yes, it's true: this man has no disc.
body: GameStop boss Ryan Cohen (last seen attempting to buy eBay ) has called for the return of physical game discs, lamenting the lack of control players have over digital purchases in a chat with Bloomberg held on the eve of Grand Theft Auto 6's release. In case you missed it, a media meteor impacted yesterday and blasted our landscape free of life. Grand Theft Auto 6 is here and—despite our Ted Litchfield's noble attempts to get you all thinking about Queen's Domain instead (you should play Queen's Domain)—it's all the world can talk about. It's also only available digitally. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop", said Cohen, remarking that players ought to be able to do with their purchased games as they will: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend". Cohen did not namecheck GTA 6 specifically, but did say that he had been speaking about this issue with all "the obvious" publishers. GameStop, of course, makes a tidy chunk of change from resales of games traded in at its stores—a segment of its business that becomes impossible to maintain in a world without physical discs for …

title: Is Niko Bellic in GTA 6?
summary: And can you go bowling with him if so?
body: Niko Bellic is one of my favorite GTA protagonists, a down-to-earth immigrant looking for a better life in Liberty City, though admittedly with a few anger issues and skeletons in his closet. Still, when people spotted that Niko's voice actor, Michael Hollick, was listed in the GTA 6 credits as "The Hitman", the rumour mill really kicked into overdrive around whether he was playing the same character. Again, if you don't want to know who Hollick plays in GTA 6, then leave now. Is Niko Bellic in GTA 6? The straight answer is, yes, Niko does appear in GTA 6 during Chapter 5: Top of the World, Ma , near the very end of the game, specifically, in the Taking Liberties mission. title: The actress who plays Mandy in GTA 6 has revealed herself: 'If you play the game, let me know if you find me'
summary: I think most players will find Mandy.
body: You'd think that everyone's favourite character in GTA 6 would be either Jason or Lucia—one of the main characters—but no, another front-runner has emerged for fans: Mandy. She's so much of a favourite, in fact, that we've had to confirm that you can't cheat on Lucia with her. You meet Mandy early on in GTA 6 when Jason visits her home to collect the rent she owes to her landlord Brian Heder and also fix her blocked sink. It's pretty apparent that she has a thing for Jason, she is his ex after all, but the feeling isn't reciprocated, no matter how much players want it to be. Things also get a little weird with her as she pushes just a little too far and suggests she's been stalking him, not a great look Mandy. But the weirdest thing of all is what Jason finds in her sink. As he's clearing out the blocked pipe he finds what looks like a severed finger. He only has it for a second before Mandy snatches it out of his hands and runs off with it, but players are pretty sure they saw what they saw. This has led some to believe that Mandy could be a serial killer. Obviously that's only one finger, and to be serial she'd need to have a whole hand at least (come on, do we not have standard…

body: World of Warcraft: Forever has a lot of changes from the classic version of the game, but one of the chief ones is that its items are different—and while I'm only just now starting to see actual, potential game-changing bits of kit (I've gotten into trinket-juggling between pulls), there have been some pretty flavourful pieces. Moon's entire philosophy seems built around flavour over form, using the example of the Ogre Loincloth, a pair of cloth casting pants with strength, as a north star of sorts: "I just want to do something different that adds texture and crunch to the game. People will see things like the Ogre Loincloth, and they'll be like: 'Why does this cloth thing have strength on it?' title: Modders reckon GTA 6 will be playable on PC within a week
summary: That's if Rockstar can't take it down first.
body: You remember when The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake launched earlier this month on Nintendo Switch 2, and it was running on PC in hours? Well, modders are claiming essentially the same will be happening for Grand Theft Auto 6, a much bigger and more complicated game. If you're wondering how these games are getting ported so quickly, it's a mixture of people dumping the game files for the public to access and, oftentimes, generative AI coding doing a lot of the grunt work of recompiling. Just yesterday, Cyberleek ( the hacking team or person who leaked GTA 6 files earlier this year) reportedly leaked the GTA 6 Xbox build , giving modders access to the game's release files. That's one important part of the porting process checked off. The only file Cyberleek says it hasn't dropped is the main executable file, and they say they will release it when their crypto coin reaches a $15 million market cap. However, Cyberleek did say they would drop the exe file on November 23 either way. summary: Would you pay $7.99 a month for one car and some in-game discounts?
body: If you preordered GTA 6 and head to the "store" page in the main menu, you'll see that you have a free month of GTA+, Rockstar's subscription service. If you didn't, you can subscribe for $7.99 a month. Yep, weird as it sounds, there's a subscription option for a singleplayer game. Subscribers to GTA+ for GTA Online get some decently sweet perks (and if you subscribe via GTA 6, you'll get them for GTAO too) like $500,000 of in-game cash every month, access to exclusive cars, multipliers on missions, discounts on in-game items, and more. But what does the GTA+ subscription get you in GTA 6? Well, how does free rides on public transportation sound? Great, right? Can I sweeten the pot with 10% off haircuts? Huh? Huh? How about if your $10 scooter rental was comped . Are you in? OK, you do also get a nice exclusive car and an extra garage to store it in. title: GTA 6 is playable in first-person, here's how to activate it
summary: I guess that's why the cars have speedometers.
body: While you can switch to first-person temporarily in Grand Theft Auto 6 when you want to get a real good close-up of a texture or when you're looking at your phone, you can't run around doing crimes and having fun like you could when GTA 5 got its first-person mode. Except actually you can, as discovered by players on Reddit and tested by our own Morgan Park. It's easy enough to activate in-game. Go to the controller settings, then under the Controller Features section change your touch pad/select button to Camera 2 / 2. Get into a car, bring up your phone with the D-pad, press Circle or B then quickly hit Select. There you go, first-person GTA 6. As Morgan's footage shows, it's completely playable. It doesn't look 100% done, however, with your shoulders clipping through the camera when you've got a longarm gun up. Seeing someone break into a car in first-person also looks a bit rough around the edges. While conspiracy theorists have convinced themselves that Rockstar is holding back this feature to sell it as DLC, I figure they're probably still polishing it to add in a future update. If you want to leave first-person, you'll have to reload a save. It doesn't have to be an old sav…

title: Help: I can't stop obeying traffic laws in GTA 6
summary: What's happening to me!?
body: A few minutes into my first play session with Grand Theft Auto 6, I was doing my first bit of driving. I'd been cruising down the Leonida Keys, and as I was patiently waiting at a red light and humming along with the radio, I had a sudden realization: I was patiently waiting at a red light. I immediately floored it, weaving into and out of oncoming traffic and channeling all the years of training in being a vehicular menace I'd been provided by prior Grands Theft Auto. But just a short way down the road, moments after blasting past a few panicked pedestrians I'd aggressively robbed of the right of way, it happened again: Without thinking, I'd come to a complete stop at a stop sign. I'm playing the world's most renowned automotive crime fantasy, and I can't stop observing the basic tenets of road safety. (Image credit: Rockstar) Repeatedly across the hours I've put into GTA 6 since launch, I've been succumbing to an embarrassing habit of obeying driverly etiquette. I'm following other drivers at a reasonable distance when I could be forcing them off the road to save time. I'm diligently staying in my lane when I could be scraping my way up the shoulder at 90 miles an hour. NPC pass…

title: GTA 6 has the best use of the PS5 controller I've ever seen
summary: The PS5 triggers are changing how I drive in GTA.
body: Six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing. They're key for Astro Bot's varied trigger-based mechanics, of course, and I wouldn't want to play Death Stranding 2 without my heavy backpack fighting back against me. But my new favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6. GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective. The resistive triggers activate when you'd expect, like while shooting guns, but they also come into play in activities that feel like they were designed around the controller: When swinging dumbbells, for instance, the triggers help me time when to release and start another rep. It's cool stuff. Rockstar's smartest use of the triggers, and one of my favorite new features of GTA 6 in general, is its two-stage throttle for vehicles : When you pull the throttle (right trigger) in any car, there's a hard resistive stop at about the 50% to 60% point. I've been call…

title: Should you give the statue to Benedict Halifax in GTA 6?
summary: In the Chapter 3 mission Dubious Provenance, should you trust, or not trust, the eccentric antiques dealer?
body: Deciding whether to give the statue to Benedict Halifax is a decision you'll need to make during the fourth story mission of Chapter 3 in GTA 6 , called Dubious Provenance. This mission will kick off after Cal visits the Bayside apartment you're borrowing from Boobie to inspect the hard drive. Once Cal leaves, you'll see an icon of a statuette at the closet door. Remember, you didn't just acquire a hard drive but a bronze statuette in Chapter 1, and if you interact with it now the mission will begin. First, you need to drive to Capri, a ritzy town on the other side of the map. At the antiques store, Evelyn Andrews tells you she isn't interested in the obviously stolen item, but art dealer Benedict Halifax approaches you on the sly and says he can have it appraised for you. Should you give the statue to him? Give the statue to Halifax : He'll give you a watch to hold onto as collateral while he appraises the statue. Then he'll vanish for a while, trying to duck you, and you'll have to call him repeatedly to track him down again. Don't give the statue to Halifax : This is really just delaying the rest of the mission. You can keep the statue for now, but if you want to progress the m…

title: In the GTA 6 Delights robbery mission, help or don't help Frankie and Mario?
summary: Frankie wants to know if you can dance, yes or no. What should you say?
body: You'll face a choice in Chapter 2 of GTA 6 , when you're ready to help Vicky rob her boss, Frankie, at the Delights strip club in Port Gellhorn. Frankie asks you an important question and you've only got a couple seconds to respond: "Can you dance? Yes or no, dude?" Frankie has caught you (as Jason) coming in the back door of the club as you and Lucia prepare to rob it. It's ladies night and one of the male strippers is out of commission, but Mario, the lead stripper, gets an idea when he meets Jason. Frankie has the same idea, and asks if Jason knows how to dance. Yes, they are asking Jason if he can fill in as a male stripper for the show. Help : If you help, Jason becomes a male stripper for the night, and yeah, it's hilarious. You dance, you strip, you grind on ladies in the crowd (including Lucia) while wearing a teeny tiny white thong, and it's just a whole lot of silly fun. And you still get to rob the place! Don't help : If you don't help, Mario walks away and the strip show is cancelled. But Frankie tries, by himself, to get the ladies worked up, performing a cringe-worthy (but funny) show on stage. Jason quickly interrupts it by putting a bullet into the ceiling and anno…

title: Where to have a bona fide bigfoot (skunk ape) sighting in GTA 6
summary: Chase down the peninsular cryptid out in the Leonida Keys.
body: One of GTA's many gags is back in GTA 6: the ol' bigfoot sighting. Well, technically I think it's a " skunk ape ," real-life Florida's maybe real-life boogeyman "cousin" to Bigfoot. Don't get that cryptid family tree twisted. How do I know it's skunk ape? I saw the thing, I swear, and there was a cloud of green stink wafting off of it. Here's exactly where it's at if you want your own smelly primate encounter. Bigfoot encounter location in GTA 6 Look for the dead end road on the west side of this peninsula. (Image credit: Rockstar) The skunk ape sighting I've found so far is just across Gambit Bay from Jason's initial house. Hop in Jason's boat on the dock outside his place and set course for the dead end road on the inside of this peninsula. Before you even make land you'll get a prompt telling you to use Focus Mode to follow the source of the noises. Hark! It's skunk ape! The creature hightails its stinky hide off into the mangrove-y woods and you'll need to keep using focus mode to chase after. You'll lose sight of it and instead find some creepy effigy thing standing beside a tree. Check it out, get stink-apacitated, and get your not so informative close-up sighting of bigfoot…

title: Cheats in GTA 6 are weirdly restrictive, and I'm counting the minutes until the PC version fixes them
summary: Unlocking a cheats menu takes dozens of hours, and even then there are still heavy restrictions.
body: Using cheats in GTA 6 is a given. GTA games are big, beautiful sandboxes of destruction, and sometimes I want to forget about story missions and just magically fill my pockets with cash, spawn a tank or a jet, and go on a rampage with infinite incendiary ammo. Naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats . But only eventually. If you were hoping to try out some cheats the moment you step into the game, I've got some bad news for you—and then some worse news. Here are the problems: You can't unlock cheats until you've completed the main story. Maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting. But then again, if you shell out potentially $100 for a game, shouldn't you be able to play it however the heck you want? I think so. GTA 6 is a big, long game, with a five chapter main story that contains 91 missions. It took me about 90 hours to finish, at which point I could finally access the cheats menu. That's where I found the next bit of bad news... You have to unlock cheats individually through milestones and challenges Congrats on playing those 90 hours: are you ready for 90 more? Most cheats on the menu are …

title: Ubisoft says Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced 'outperformed expectations,' lays off 166 more people anyway
summary: Ubisoft Montreal and Quebec are the latest to fall under the axe.
body: Ubisoft has laid off 166 people from its offices in Montreal and Quebec City, saying in a statement provided to PC Gamer that its "production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs." Founded in 1997, Ubisoft Montreal is one of the biggest game studios in the world, with roughly 4,000 employees as of 2022. Ubisoft Quebec, launched in 2005, is somewhat smaller but still substantial: Its website says the studio has "a team of over 600 creative, passionate, and innovative talents." The cuts reportedly impact employees who could not be assigned elsewhere after their existing projects were cancelled or rescoped. Whatever the reason, it's bleak: This is the latest round in a series of layoffs that have battered the company since it announced a major restructuring in January, which followed years of struggles including workplace misconduct scandals, persistent difficulties getting games launched , and underperformance among big releases. Ubisoft said in today's half-year financial report report that it's reduced its headcount by roughly 1,100 people over the past six months…

title: Even our bunch of diehard PC gamers aren't that bothered by 30 fps in GTA 6
summary: The game wears it surprisingly well, though we'll be less happy if the PC version is similarly capped.
body: For a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer. Yes, if you try to insult XCOM, you're going to get a slap, but we've only just started playing GTA 6 ( well, some of us ) and we're mostly over the whole 'only runs at 30 fps' thing already. It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well. GTA 6 certainly does that. That's the impression I get from most members of the team that have played it so far. Though if Rockstar is listening, when you do get around to our precious PC version, we'd love nothing more than 4K60—maybe more. James Bentley, Hardware Writer (Image credit: Future) I will no doubt appreciate frames above 100 fps when GTA 6 comes to PC. Heck, I'd even just appreciate going up to 60 fps. But in my handful of hours with the game thus far, I just have simply not been that bothered by it. title: Yes, you're hearing 'Weird Al' Yankovic hosting a radio station in GTA 6
summary: Also hosting are Lana Del Rey, Bad Bunny, Keith Richards, and—for some reason—Jeremy Irons.
body: If you're one of the countless millions contributing to the collective endangering of global productivity by enjoying Grand Theft Auto 6 at launch, you might have paused in the middle of blatantly disregarding traffic laws to wonder: Wait a second, am I hearing "Weird Al" Yankovic hosting this pretend radio station? And yes, you are: In a Bluesky post earlier today, the beloved comedic musician and polka maestro confirmed that he offered his voice for DJ Al, who hosts '80s music station Vice City FM alongside Swedish actress, model, and singer Brigitte Nielsen. Their contributions were then double-confirmed by the full GTA 6 credits , which Rockstar published once launch time hit. I’m the host of GTA 6’s “non-stop ‘80s” radio channel Vice City FM. title: I just found a verrrry familiar-looking hat in GTA 6, and it was in the last place I would have expected
summary: Sometimes it pays to follow signs.
body: I just found a curious artifact of the Old West in GTA 6, and the best part is I stumbled across it completely by accident. That's right, partner: Arthur Morgan's cowboy hat is in Grand Theft Auto 6, and you won't find it in some trendy Western fashion shop or in a McMansion as part of a wealthy crypto bro's collection. If you want to wear it yourself, I'll tell you below where you can find it. How to find Arthur Morgan's cowboy hat (Image credit: Rockstar Games) I was out in Port Gellhorn looking for a particular kind of car for reasons completely unrelated to clothing accessories. While I was driving, I spotted a sign on the side of the road with a balloon tied to it, reading "Yard Sale" with an arrow pointing down the road. I followed the sign which led to more yard sale signs and, yup, sure enough, the signs pointed me to an actual yard sale. And among the items for sale was a very familiar-looking hat. It's called a "Genuine Cowboy Hat" and, this being a yard sale, it only cost $5. But I knew the second I saw it that this was no ordinary cowboy hat. Here, have a look at it from the back. (Image credit: Rockstar Games) Yep. No mistaking that. I even got a little pang of sadnes…

title: As a PC gamer, of course the first thing I did in GTA 6 was try a mouse and keyboard
summary: We also gave steering wheels a go, too.
body: I am nothing if not entirely predictable. I've waited 13 years to play a new Grand Theft Auto game and the first thing I do when I finally get around to booting GTA 6 —and definitely not spoofing my home address to access it early—is jam a mouse and keyboard into my Xbox Series X just to see. GTA 5, once it made its way to PC, was always a game I played both with a keyboard and mouse and with a controller plugged in. Keeb and rodent for shooting, especially in the first-person mode, and the controller for just getting about in the game world. It was a real best of both worlds kinda thing that the PC does so well. It was the same with Red Dead Redemption 2, a game I completely avoided until it finally came to the PC. Keyboard and mouse for runnin' and gunnin' and a controller for horsin' around. Yeehaw. So, I was hoping—hoping against hope, really—that I could just do the same with GTA 6. I was hoping that I could just plug in my little Mountain keyboard and my DeathAdder mouse, and it would just work. Sadly no, there is no mouse and keyboard support for GTA 6. There is for Xbox, and my keyboard works fine just in the home screens, but as soon as you hit the game itself… nada. Keyb…

title: 'I'm all about the heist': 43 soldiers re-enlisted in the US army to get a 4-day weekend to play GTA 6
summary: That's one way to get a long weekend.
body: We got confirmation a couple of months ago that the US Army's 3rd Infantry Division was offering a four-day pass to play Grand Theft Auto 6 for soldiers who re-enlist for at least two years. And now the time has come to collect. Talking to Task & Purpose one soldier who took advantage of the program, Sgt. Jamire Smith, described how he's planning to spend the long weekend: "I'm all campaign. I’m all about the heist. I think I have a good 24 hours to waste on it. (Image credit: Rockstar) "I was actually in the process of getting out, I was towards my final stages of getting out … but my company and the battalion helped me navigate through that and they showed me that there’s still a need for me, and that I am still a clear and value asset to the team, and so that’s really what drove me to say 'let’s keep going, let’s keep driving'. Maybe be a lifer in this, since I already made it my career." In total 43 soldiers re-enlisted through the GTA 6 incentive, an idea that was born from Staff Sgt. Brittany Wolfer.
